title: Baer v. Illiana Presbytery
disposition_detail: Appeal denied. Issue A: No—the Presbytery did not err in the sustained charge that Baer violated the 9th commandment, the 4th and 7th ordination vows, and the 3rd installation vow by saying the Session had 'demanded' his resignation for six weeks. Issue B: No—no irregularities, prejudice, or due-process violation warranted reversal. The lower court had not sustained the other remaining charge; its guilt judgment and indefinite suspension until repentance remained.
first_summary: The SJC denied an appeal by a pastor who was indefinitely suspended after being convicted of violating the Ninth Commandment and ordination vows by saying the Session had 'demanded' his resignation for six weeks. The SJC found no error in the conviction or censure and no due-process violation, deferring to the Presbytery's factual findings and judgment under BCO 39-3.
summary: An appeal from a Presbytery judgment and indefinite suspension of a pastor turned on whether he violated the Ninth Commandment and ordination/installation vows by telling the congregation the Session had 'demanded' his resignation for six weeks. The SJC denied the appeal, holding the Session as a whole had not formally demanded resignation; individual elders' earlier opinions did not excuse the overstatement, which harmed the Session's good name. It also found no due-process irregularity or prejudice warranting reversal, deferring to the lower court under BCO 39-3, leaving indefinite suspension in place.

sources.supports: Canonical case identity, SJC appeal posture, issues, judgment, reasoning, and roll-call adoption of the denial.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Lines 1-3, 9, 112-128: the case is 1998-09, Baer v. Illiana Presbytery, decided by the SJC at the 28th General Assembly (2000) with disposition denied. The decision was written by RE John H. Van Voorhis with concurrence of TE Charles E. McGowan and RE Edward J. Robeson; the Judicial Panel recommended denial to the SJC and the roll call shows 19 concur, 2 recused, 3 absent.
evidence_notes.dispute: Lines 13-41, 48, 55: Pastor Baer's conflict with the youth pastor and Session led to a Session request for resignation; the congregation did not give the required two-thirds, but Session petitioned Presbytery, which investigated, suspended him, dissolved the pastoral relationship, and prosecuted charges. After withdrawals, an invalid charge, and guilty pleas to five charges, the Judicial Commission sustained one remaining charge—that Baer violated the 9th commandment, 4th and 7th ordination vows, and 3rd installation vow by saying the Session had 'demanded' his resignation for six weeks—and imposed indefinite suspension until repentance. Baer appealed.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Lines 57-113: Issues were (A) whether Presbytery erred in that conviction and (B) whether irregularities, prejudice, or due-process violations required reversal. The SJC answered No to both and denied the appeal. On A, although individual elders had earlier urged resignation, the Session as a whole took no formal action until after the congregational meeting; Baer's repeated 'demanded' statement was an overstatement harming the Session's good name, and he admitted it was emotionally charged. On B, the SJC found no improperly withheld material or substantial missing evidence, tolerated minor record flaws, and applied BCO 39-3 deference to the lower court's factual and discretionary judgments.
evidence_notes.qualifications: Lines 48, 83-84, 92-93, 109-113: the SJC noted it could not review an August 26, 1998 judgment/censure not in the ROC; it said the parties' ongoing relationship was outside the case; it did not find all record-keeping perfect, only that flaws were not reversible. The denial left the indefinite suspension until repentance undisturbed.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: Line 48 and lines 41, 55: the SJC refers to the lower court's Judicial Commission judgment/censure of August 26, 1998 but states the ROC contains no record of it and that related September 3, 1998 Presbytery minutes were not before the SJC. The appeal concerns the Presbytery's October 17, 1998 approval and censure; no separate SJC decision is incorporated by reference.
